walkthroughs.body_html: The heart has four chambers: two atria on top, two ventricles below. The right side handles deoxygenated blood; the left side handles oxygenated blood. The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood around the whole body.

Four valves keep blood moving forward: tricuspid (right atrium to right ventricle), bicuspid/mitral (left atrium to left ventricle) and two semilunar valves at the exits to the pulmonary artery and aorta.

Arteries carry blood away from the heart — thick muscular walls, high pressure. Veins return blood to the heart — thinner walls, valves, low pressure. Capillaries are one cell thick for exchange of oxygen, nutrients and waste.
